summary:
The design is sound in substance and can ship. The verdict for the three tests, the counter correction, the redirect, the deepest-first reorder and the never-skipped Facts all rest on measurements, and I checked the design's code claims against the tree:
- Scanner.cs:175-191: the walk counts a parent before it opens any child.
- SynchronousIoCancel.cs:492/522: KeptLastAccess is reset only at Open.
- LongPath.cs:44: the scan root's trailing separators are trimmed.
- The rule-2 patterns match nothing in Core.Tests today.

The first must-verify precondition (tree d) is already implied by data. In spike 1's unpatched control, tree (d) gave (2,1) with R unmoved, and the successful-open rule removes nothing there. So kept is 1, which is the truth.

There is one major finding. Rule 2 forbids literal %SystemRoot%\Temp spellings but not Path.GetTempPath(). That call is the route that actually put fixtures there, and CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:282 already uses it. As a result, the redirect is enforced only for tests that remember to use TempTree.

The minor findings:
- The %SystemRoot% comparison has to be in \\?\ form, the way NormalizeSyncRoots does it. The design leaves this out, and spike 1 had to strip the prefix.
- Rule 1 cannot see the skip-at-discovery attribute that the acceptance test itself uses. It also largely duplicates CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped.
- The contract text says "moved", but the correction is a structural rule, not an observation.
- The material mutation check runs in a scratch copy (CC-004), even though spikes 1 and 3 already measured both mutations.
- The trailing-separator Theory row cannot reach the branch it names.
- Four extras: key the set by entry index, TempTree.Outside under the explicit-root constructor, the "unfindable leftover" premise, and path aliases.

findings.claim: Architecture rule 2 ('no Core test builds a fixture in %SystemRoot%\Temp except the deliberate one') only bans literal spellings: SpecialFolder.Windows+"Temp", "C:\Windows\Temp" and %SystemRoot%/%windir%. This slice's bug came by a different route: a fixture rooted at Path.GetTempPath() while the engine's TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. The rule does not ban that. The redirect lives only in TempTree, so any test that calls Path.GetTempPath() directly still lands in %SystemRoot%\Temp under the engine, and rule 2 passes it. One file does this today: CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:282 (SyncRootRig, which spike 4 found failing 4/4 for exactly this reason). The invariant holds only while every future fixture remembers to use TempTree, and that is the same remembering that left three tests red through six validations.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:282. .taad/fitness.yaml:1144-1158, the rule as the engine already appended it. TempTree.cs:17 is the only place the redirect will live. Spike temptree-redirect-out-of-systemroot, constraint 1: SyncRootRig takes Path.GetTempPath() directly.
findings.fix: Add the pattern `Path\.GetTempPath\s*\(` to rule 2's must_not_match. Add except_files for TempTree.cs, FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs (:388 takes only the drive root) and CloudPlaceholderTests.cs, and give CloudPlaceholderTests.cs a comment pointing at the filed 'route SyncRootRig/CloudRig through TempTree' slice, which removes that exemption. The redirect then holds by construction for every new Core test.
findings.class_of: routes into %SystemRoot%\Temp that bypass TempTree's redirect

findings.claim:
The design tests the location with Scanner's existing IsAtOrUnder 'against Environment.GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.Windows) computed once per scan'.
- IsAtOrUnder compares raw prefixes and documents that both arguments are \\?\ paths (Scanner.cs:84). Every folder path in the walk is \\?\-form (LongPath.Child of win32Root).
- GetFolderPath returns 'C:\WINDOWS' with no prefix. Taken literally, the design makes IsAtOrUnder false for every folder, so the correction never fires and the acceptance test stays at 7 vs 4.
- The sync-root precedent the design cites normalises its roots first through LongPath.NormalizeRoot (Scanner.cs:104). Spike 1's patch also had to strip \\?\ before comparing.
- If GetFolderPath ever returned an empty string, a naive ToExtended would give '\\?\', which matches every path.
findings.evidence: Scanner.cs:84-87 (IsAtOrUnder contract), :104 (NormalizeSyncRoots), :349 (child paths); spike kept-counter-uncounts-parent-of-child-keep-open-under-system, PATCH paragraph: '(\\?\ prefix stripped, case-insensitive ordinal prefix...)'
findings.fix: State it in the Scanner component: hold %SystemRoot% as LongPath.NormalizeRoot(Environment.GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.Windows)).Win32, computed once in Run the way NormalizeSyncRoots does. If GetFolderPath returns empty, apply no correction.

findings.claim:
Rule 1 ('the Windows-folder last-access tests are never skipped') covers only LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs. It cannot see the skip mechanism the slice's own acceptance test uses, which is the template a builder copies.
- That mechanism is a custom FactAttribute subclass that sets Skip in its constructor when %SystemRoot%\Temp is not writable.
- If such an attribute is defined in a helper file and used as [WindowsTempFact], rule 1's `Skip\s*=` never sees it, and neither does CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped, whose pattern needs `[Fact(`/`[Theory(` with Skip inside.
- Rule 1's Trait clause names only Network|Cloud, but under the default-suite guard any Trait means an excluded opt-in.
- Apart from those two gaps, rule 1 duplicates CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped (fitness.yaml:129-136), which already covers this file, and it lacks that rule's Explicit pattern.
findings.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-096-LastAccessUnderWindowsTemp/LastAccessUnderWindowsTempTests.cs:61-70 and :76 ([WindowsTempFact]). .taad/fitness.yaml:129-136 (existing rule over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/**/*.cs) and :1132-1139 (rule 1). A grep found no custom Fact/Theory attribute in Core.Tests today.
findings.fix: In rule 1, replace the Network|Cloud clause with `\[\s*Trait\s*\(` (no Trait at all), and add `\[\s*(?!Fact\b|Theory\b)\w+(Fact|Theory)\b` so the file uses only the stock attributes. Optionally add `:\s*(FactAttribute|TheoryAttribute)\b` to the existing Core.Tests-wide never-skipped rule; it matches nothing today.
findings.class_of: ways to take the Windows-folder Facts out of the default run

findings.claim:
The new LastAccessKept contract text and the contracts block both say kept = 'minus folders at or under %SystemRoot% whose last access the scan's own later keep-open of a child folder moved'. The rule as specified observes nothing. It removes a parent whenever io.KeptLastAccess is true for a child, and that flag means the -1 set succeeded. It diverges from 'moved' in both directions:
(i) Under-count: the parent is removed although nothing moved, when its stored last access is within NTFS's ~1 h window or last-access updates are off.
(ii) Over-count: the parent is not removed when the child's FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES CreateFile succeeded but the -1 set then failed. TryOpenKeepingLastAccess returns false there and falls back to a plain open, but the write-class open has already stamped the parent.
The tests back-date by 48 h, so neither shows. The text overstates what the counter knows.
findings.evidence: SynchronousIoCancel.cs:532-542: kept is true only if SetFileInformationByHandle succeeds after the write-attributes CreateFile; otherwise the handle is disposed and false is returned. Design contract 'ScanResult.LastAccessKept', notes: 'minus folders ... that the scan's own later successful keep-open of a child folder moved'.
findings.fix: Word the contract as the rule: kept = asked folders whose keep-open succeeded, minus each folder at or under %SystemRoot% that has a child folder whose keep-open succeeded. Add that on this machine such an open was measured to move the parent, and that the counter does not read times back. Record (ii) as a known gap rather than adding a flag.

findings.evidence: Design case 'the Scanner correction is reverted' (material: true; its check is a scratch copy). Contract 'Mutation check of the Windows-folder Facts'. Spike combined-redirect-deepest-first-counter-fix (c) d1-d3. Spike kept-counter-uncounts-parent-of-child-keep-open-under-system, tree (d).
findings.fix: Mark the case non-material, settled by spike 3 (d1-d3) and spike 1 (tree d), and keep the failure messages that name each direction. Or, if a standing mutant is wanted, commit it as a script. Do not leave it as a build obligation discharged in a scratch copy.

findings.claim: Material case 4 and the Theory's 'trailing separator' row claim to catch a parent string normalised differently from the root ('kept reads 5 against 4'). That branch is unreachable. Scanner.Scan runs LongPath.NormalizeRoot, which trims trailing separators from every root except a drive root, before ListRoot or the set sees it. So the row produces the same win32Root as the 'as-is' row and can never fail for the reason it names (CC-005: an earlier step short-circuits the targeted branch). The spelling risk that is real, the \\?\ form of %SystemRoot% (m1), is already caught by every row.
findings.evidence: LongPath.cs:21-46 (NormalizeRoot; :44 TrimSeparators; the \\?\ branch at :31-34 is trimmed too). Scanner.cs:62 (Scan normalises before Run). Design case 'the scan root is given with a trailing backslash'.
findings.fix: Drop the trailing-separator row, or keep it labelled as a redundant spelling check, not a material case. Rest the lower-case row's material status on the case-insensitive comparison, which is real.

findings.claim:
The taste disagreement over parent identity rejects 'a per-folder flag or index carried by the walk' because it 'changes the walk's work items'. That premise is wrong.
- Each work item already carries the folder's store entry ((int folder, string path, int row), Scanner.cs:175).
- The store already records every entry's parent (_store.Parent, Scanner.cs:419), and the root is entry 0 (:423).
- A HashSet<int> keyed by entry index, with the parent found as _store.Parent(folder), needs no change to the work items. It drops the string derivation (trim, cut at the last separator, keep the 'form CountListingOpen received') and its spelling questions.
Only the %SystemRoot% location test still needs a path.
findings.evidence: Scanner.cs:175 (work-item tuple), :349 (push with entry index), :419-423 (Parent; root is entry 0). Design taste disagreement 6 and the key decision 'Track only kept folders ... keyed by the path'.
findings.fix: Optional: key the per-scan set by store entry index (the root as 0, counted in ListRoot before AppendRoot) and find the parent via _store.Parent(folder). Otherwise, record in the design that the stated cost of the alternative was mistaken.

findings.claim: The new internal TempTree(string testsRoot) constructor sets Root under the given root. TempTree.Outside() still builds its 'folder beside the tree' under the static TestsRoot, which is the user's TEMP. A caller of the explicit-root constructor that uses Outside(), as HeldOpenTreeTests does for its control folder, therefore gets a 'sibling' in a different folder, outside luafv's reach. Keeping Outside beside Root is left to remembering.
findings.evidence: TempTree.cs:17 (static TestsRoot), :61-67 (Outside uses TestsRoot), :29 (Root = TestsRoot + id). HeldOpenTreeTests.cs:226 (_tree.Outside("control")).
findings.fix: Store the chosen tests root in an instance field set by both constructors, and build Outside() from it.

findings.claim:
The design rests the 'tree gone' case, and the taste disagreement over whether default-suite Facts should write to C:\Windows\Temp at all, on the premise that a leftover there 'could never be found'. That premise is false for where the Facts build. They use C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests\<guid>, and this user can list and watch fsa-tests:
- spike 4 ran a FileSystemWatcher on it and listed 0 entries afterwards;
- spike 3 counted it at 0 entries before and after.
Only direct children of C:\Windows\Temp are unlistable: the bug test's fsa-sl096-<guid> and the survey's leftover. A leftover from the Facts can be found by name and removed.
findings.evidence: Spike temptree-redirect-out-of-systemroot ('Across all 5 watched runs there were 0 Created or POLL events under C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests, and the folder had 0 entries afterwards'; 'the session token cannot list or watch C:\Windows\Temp itself'). Spike combined-redirect-deepest-first-counter-fix ('C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests existed before and after with 0 entries'). Design case 'clean up a test tree built in C:\Windows\Temp'.
findings.fix: Correct the rationale: the unrecoverable case applies only to the unchanged bug test. Optionally have validate list C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests and report any GUID folder left behind, which is a measurable leftover check.

findings.claim: The %SystemRoot% location test is lexical, a prefix match on the root as the person spelled it. A root under C:\Windows reached through another spelling skips the correction entirely: a subst drive letter (the project already uses SUBST in V-001), a junction or mount point, or a \\?\GLOBALROOT/volume-GUID path. Whether luafv still stamps parents when the folder is opened through such a name is unmeasured. It acts on the opened file object, so it plausibly does, and kept would then over-count again. The counter is internal (Q-103, Q-159), so the consequence is small. It is the same 'matched by spelling' limit SL-095 recorded for the layer store.
findings.evidence: Scanner.cs:85-87 (lexical IsAtOrUnder). LongPath.NormalizeRoot does not resolve reparse points or subst. Lesson SL-095: 'Layer store is matched by path spelling; only GetFinalPathNameByHandleW is spelling-independent'.
findings.fix: Record the limit in the ScanResult contract text and the triage doc. If it ever matters, compare the root's final path, from one GetFinalPathNameByHandleW on the root handle ListRoot already holds.
findings.class_of: root spellings that escape a lexical location guard

dimensions_checked.result:
Must-verify 1 (tree d) is effectively settled. In spike 1's unpatched control, tree (d) gave (2,1) with R unmoved, and with the successful-open rule no child keep-open succeeds there, so it removes nothing: kept 1 equals the truth.

Must-verify 2 (Windows 10, ProgramData/ProgramFiles), if false:
- Where luafv does not move parents (Windows 10, EnableLUA=0, or a later build), the location-keyed correction under-counts (kept 4 against 7 unmoved), and Fact (1) turns the default suite red. That is an intended canary, but there is no runtime guard, so the product counter is wrong on that machine until someone acts.
- If luafv does act in ProgramData/ProgramFiles, kept over-counts there and no Fact sees it.

Recalled -1 claim checked: NtDoc's FILE_BASIC_INFORMATION (https://ntdoc.m417z.com/file_basic_information, citing Microsoft's wdm page) says '-1 ... time stamp updates are disabled for I/O operations performed on the file handle', which supports the design. The Russinovich source exists (TechNet Magazine, 'Inside Windows Vista User Account Control', https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/technet-magazine/cc138019(v=msdn.10)), but the extract did not include the namespace sentence. It is not load-bearing, because scope is limited to the measured %SystemRoot%.

The premise that a leftover there is unrecoverable is wrong for fsa-tests (m8).

- The correction diverges from 'moved' in both directions: a recent parent is removed although it did not move, and a write-attributes open that succeeds before the -1 set fails leaves the parent counted (m3).
- Root path aliases (subst, junction) escape the location test (m9).
- An empty GetFolderPath would match everything once given the \\?\ prefix (folded into m1).
- Cancel, the excluded store, remote and cloud folders all stay behind the existing gates; that was checked in the code at Scanner.cs:182-191 and :279-289.

- The redirect is enforced only for fixtures that use TempTree; Path.GetTempPath() bypasses it (M1).
- TempTree.Outside ignores the explicit root (m7).
- An entry-index key would remove the string parent derivation (m6).

- Rule 1 largely duplicates CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped (fitness.yaml:129-136), which already covers the same file (folded into m2).
- The refusal for a SYSTEM-profile redirect target covers a scenario nobody has measured, but it is one branch and cheap.
- Otherwise lean: no read-back pass, no luafv detection, no KnownWorkarounds entry. That is proportionate for an internal counter (Q-103, Q-159).

- The %SystemRoot% comparison needs the \\?\ form, which the design does not state (m1).
- The LastAccessKept contract claims an observed move where the code applies a structural rule (m3).

- ChooseTestsRoot throwing inside TempTree's static initializer makes every TempTree test fail with a TypeInitializationException that carries the named cause. That is acceptable.
- TempTree.Dispose throwing in a using block masks the original assertion. This is existing behaviour.
- The unchanged bug test swallows a failed cleanup in the unlistable C:\Windows\Temp (Remove at :157-172). That is out of scope, but it is the one remaining unfindable-leftover path.
- No new error path in the Scanner.

- Spike 3's 'kept 4 of 7' carries over to the successful-open rule on tree (b): every child keep-open succeeds there, so the two rules remove the same parents.
- Spike 1's patch stripped \\?\ before comparing, and the design omits that (m1).
- Reading 'Counting-rule tests build real NTFS trees in %TEMP%' as the user's HKCU TEMP is defensible, and the design flags it rather than hiding it.
- No contradiction with the answered questions Q-103, Q-159, Q-186 or Q-192.

- Rule 2 misses Path.GetTempPath() (M1).
- Rule 1 misses a custom skip attribute and any Trait other than Network|Cloud (m2).
- CC-002: both rules are settled (Fitness only, no xUnit twin), which matches the project's settled-rule practice.
- A grep of rule 2's patterns over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests found no hits today.
- Builder caution: TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls has including_comments: true over src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/** with `\b(File|Directory|...)\.`. New ScanResult/Scanner comments that cite Directory.SetLastAccessTimeUtc or File.* would trip it.

- The material mutation check is a scratch-copy procedure, against CC-004 (m4).
- The trailing-separator row cannot reach its stated branch (m5).
- The acceptance bug test skips itself at discovery where %SystemRoot%\Temp is not writable, and a skip exits 0. Validate should read 'Passed: 1', not just exit 0; the never-skipped Facts cover this in the default suite.
- Otherwise the cases trace through without early aborts: preconditions read with read-class opens, and the deny ACE is set before back-dating.

none. The only writes are test trees in folders this user created under C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. There is no elevation, the deny ACE is restored before delete, and no product access mask or open changes.
